pcssri-pop-4.title: SSRI sexual dysfunction
lines: In practice: sexual dysfunction in more than half of patients
Most common type: difficulty reaching orgasm

pcssri-pop-6.title: Citalopram QT precautions
lines: Avoid in: congenital long QT syndrome, bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, uncompensated heart failure
Monitor: potassium, magnesium in patients at risk of low levels

pcssri-pop-7.title: Late-pregnancy exposure
lines: > ↑ risk of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
> some newborns need prolonged hospitalization, respiratory support, tube feeding

pcssri-pop-8.title: Adequate trial
lines: Full dose: 6 weeks before considering a change

pctca-pop-1.title: Tertiary and secondary amines
lines: Tertiary amines: more serotonin reuptake blockade; more anticholinergic, more sedating
Secondary amines: more norepinephrine reuptake blockade; less anticholinergic, less sedating

pctca-pop-2.title: Similarity to class IA antiarrhythmics
lines: Na⁺ channel blockade: similar to class IA antiarrhythmics such as quinidine

pctca-pop-3.title: Line of therapy for pain and headache
lines: Neuropathic pain: first-line TCA or gabapentinoid
Chronic tension headache: first-line amitriptyline for prevention
TCAs: also used for diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome, fibromyalgia

pctca-pop-4.title: Doxepin for insomnia
lines: Low-dose doxepin Silenor: approved for sleep-maintenance insomnia

pctca-pop-6.title: Seizure risk
lines: Clomipramine: seizure is the most significant risk
Serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs): serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake blockade → dose-dependent ↑ blood pressure
Onset: within days of an abrupt stop
Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), SNRIs: first line for generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, posttraumatic stress disorder
Avoid during: abrupt withdrawal from alcohol, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, antiepileptics
Erection lasting over 4 hours: urologic emergency
